description: Una is a self-hosted Wispr Flow replacement: hold a hotkey anywhere, speak, and clean text lands in the focused app. Everything runs on your own hardware and it LoRA-fine-tunes Whisper on your voice the longer you use it.
features: Push-to-talk dictation from any app via global hotkey
Local Whisper transcription via faster-whisper with CUDA
Local LLM cleanup for filler, punctuation, and per-app tone
One-click Fix-up polish via yagami LLM with model settings
Automatic correction capture from pasted text for training pairs
Review queue and correction editor with audio playback
Custom dictionary injected into decoding and cleanup prompts
LoRA voice fine-tuning of Whisper with WER-gated hot-swap
QLoRA style fine-tuning of cleanup LLM on polished pairs
Personal style LoRA with Claude teacher drafts
Model registry with evaluation history and one-click rollback
Dashboard for transcripts, dictionary, training, and usage insights
History main window with Settings button for smaller window
Racing multi-address server list with makima and mDNS discovery
Hold, toggle, hybrid modes with left/right modifiers, shortcut abort, tray and HUD
iPhone app on TestFlight: record, upload, corrections, keyboard mic dictation

desktop-windows.summary: Tauri WebviewWindows for history (main home window), settings (small separate window), review, transient HUD pill and correction popup, built as Svelte 5 pages with Svelte runes state. Multi-page Vite build emits app/history, settings, review, hud, and correction entries mounted by per-window main.ts files; History.svelte is a sidebar shell with persistent dashboard iframe for server pages plus local Review, while Settings.svelte lives in its own window opened from the history sidebar Settings button. Strict monochrome design system in src/lib/tokens.css plus shared src/lib/ui.css controls (Geist type, hairline borders, no accent color, filled-vs-ring status dots); all windows talk to Rust only via Tauri invoke/listen and postMessage handshake with the embedded dashboard.

rules: Keep windows independent: one Svelte root per html entry defined in vite.config.ts; do not merge HUD pill or correction popup into the Una window.
Do not redefine backend shapes in UI: types.ts mirrors una-core serde output, so update it when Rust changes.
HUD must stay transparent and theme-independent; only typeface and accent are shared.
Correction window must be immediately typeable on open (focus textarea, caret at end) and Escape must record nothing.

No color anywhere and no theme picker: status is filled dot (fine) vs ring (needs attention), windows follow the OS colour scheme; use tokens.css variables, never colored text, buttons, dots or per-window colors.

Native hotkey bindings carry the platform's own keycodes (macOS virtual keycodes, X11 keycodes on Linux): keycaps.ts picks its keycode tables, bottom row and modifier list by IS_MAC; never compare a native keycode against the other platform's table.

Dashboard server pages — embedded via iframe in Dashboard.svelte with postMessage navigation, embed mode (no sidebar, follows system theme), and offline retry state

desktop-shell.summary: The desktop shell is the Tauri v2 Rust host for the menu-bar dictation client: it owns app startup, shared AppState, Tauri commands, and bridging of una-core controller effects to windows, audio, network, and injection. It now owns two windows again — the history window as the main home window (Home/Review/Dictionary/Training/Insights plus a Settings button) and the smaller settings window — plus separate Review Dictations and HUD/correction windows. A newcomer must grasp that all dictation logic lives in una-core's FSM; this layer only runs its EffectRunner, forwards snapshots, and manages windows.

flows.name: Dictation turn
steps: Hotkey press or tray toggle sends Command to controller (main.rs hotkey handler, tray.rs, commands.rs)
Controller FSM emits effects; TauriEffects runs them: audio engine, endpoint resolve, ApiClient upload (effects.rs)
State snapshots forwarded as state-changed events to HUD webview, tray label, HUD interactivity (events.rs)
On success Done cue plays, text injected, last_dictation stored and correction watch armed (effects.rs, corrections.rs, app_state.rs)

flows.name: Correction after paste
steps: Upload result sets last_dictation; insert effect consumes it once paste lands (app_state.rs, effects.rs)
Watch window: no edit key yields accepted signal; edit in readable app reads field back and diffs pasted span yielding edited (corrections.rs)
Unreadable-app edit opens focused correction window (windows.rs accessory-mode flip)
Correction command reports result to server for training set (commands.rs, corrections.rs)

flows.name: Settings rebind
steps: Webview calls set_config command with validation of hotkey mode, hud_mode, server URLs (commands.rs)
Persisted config updates shared RwLock and EndpointResolver (app_state.rs, commands.rs)
hotkey::apply tears down old registration and registers combo or native backend (hotkey.rs)
Windows adjust HUD visibility mode and tray launch-at-login state (windows.rs, tray.rs)

client-core.summary: Shared platform-agnostic Rust core for the desktop dictation client: dictation state machine plus audio capture, server HTTP client, endpoint selection, config, spool, discovery, and IPC. Built around a pure deterministic FSM in state.rs with a tokio Controller actor executing Effects; audio runs on a dedicated cpal worker thread resampled to 16kHz mono. Newcomers must grasp that state.rs owns all timing/transitions and everything else is an effect runner around it.

map.name: Server HTTP client (dictation upload, health, correction)

flows.name: Dictation utterance
steps: Controller receives Command (Toggle/Start) via mpsc or ipc socket
step() advances Machine and emits Effects with at-timestamps
EffectRunner starts audio worker capture with warm stream reuse
Audio finalized to 16kHz mono WAV, level frames on watch channel
EndpointResolver picks cached/probed base URL
ApiClient POSTs multipart dictation with utterance_id, one retry on connect/reset only
On failure spool WAV to cache dir; Snapshot broadcast on each change

flows.name: Endpoint resolution
steps: Collect ordered candidate URLs (manual URL wins over discovery)
Probe candidates concurrently with per-candidate timeout
First health success wins and is cached for CACHE_TTL
Steady-state dictations use lock-read cached endpoint
Invalidate cache on upload failure for roaming

flows.name: Correction capture
steps: Record pasted span range and post-paste text
Accessibility path recovers edited span via edited_region_text or returns None if outside span
Keystroke path tracks span length via EditCounter, invalidated by clicks/arrows/undo
PUT correction to /v1/dictations/{id}/correction for training pair

client/crates/una-core/src/audio.rs — cpal capture worker, 16kHz resampling, level metering, WAV encoding, warm keepalive
client/crates/una-core/src/net.rs — server API client: multipart upload, health, correction PUT, timeouts and retry rule
client/crates/una-core/src/endpoint.rs — concurrent candidate probing, cached winner, TTL and invalidate
client/crates/una-core/src/config.rs — TOML config, server/discovery settings, Binding combo vs native keycode
client/crates/una-core/src/correction.rs — edited_region_text and EditCounter pure correction logic
client/crates/una-core/src/spool.rs — cache-dir WAV spool, newest KEEP=5 pruning, duplicate suppression
client/crates/una-core/src/discovery.rs — _una._tcp.local mDNS browse, DiscoveredServer with version/api TXT
client/crates/una-core/src/lib.rs — crate root re-exporting Controller, Machine, Effects, EndpointResolver
rules: Never put timing or IO inside step(): all timestamps travel in Events; caller executes Effects.
Discard utterances under MIN_UTTERANCE (300ms); auto-finalize at MAX_UTTERANCE (5min); Done dismisses after DONE_DISMISS (900ms).
Audio must be 16kHz mono s16le WAV (TARGET_SAMPLE_RATE); cpal stream stays on its worker thread, never Send.
Retry uploads exactly once on connect/reset with same utterance_id; never retry on HTTP status errors.
Manually configured server URL always beats autodiscovery; discovery only when url empty and autodiscover true.
Spool keeps newest 5 only and must not stack duplicates of a re-spooled retry.
edges: Desktop shell — drives Controller via Commands and executes Effects (hotkey, tray, windows, sounds, paste)
Platform inject — performs text paste/reading that correction.rs measures and the FSM triggers
CLI — drives dictation remotely through unix-socket IPC toggle/start/stop/cancel
Server API — target of net.rs multipart dictation, health checks, and correction PUTs
Server services — consumes uploaded WAVs; discovery TXT version/api describes its capability

platform-inject.summary: OS text injection, focused-app access and single-key hotkeys behind the traits in lib.rs so core and the shell stay platform-agnostic. macOS injects via NSPasteboard save/restore plus a CGEvent Cmd+V chord, reads/edits fields via AX AXValue, and captures hotkeys on an active CGEventTap. Linux selects X11 (XTest, with one long-lived arboard clipboard) vs Wayland (ydotool, else wtype, else clipboard-only) by env vars, and on X11 hears single-key hotkeys through XInput2 raw key events (keytap.rs); una_platform::hotkeys names whichever tap the platform has.

map.name: Linux single-key hotkeys and key recorder (XInput2 raw keys)

flows.name: macOS inject text
steps: Caller invokes TextInjector with InjectOptions via lib.rs trait
mod.rs saves pasteboard (skipped past 10MB) and sets transient marker
mod.rs places dictation text on NSPasteboard
mod.rs synthesizes Cmd+V CGEvent chord (layout-resolved V keycode, fallback 9)
axtext.rs optionally snapshots focused AXValue for later edit detection
mod.rs restores saved pasteboard, returns Injected or ClipboardOnly

flows.name: macOS hotkey match
steps: EventTap runs CFRunLoop with active HID tap on keyDown/keyUp/flagsChanged
set_binding registers target keycode from keys.rs tables
Matching keyDown/keyUp is consumed (Drop) and reported via on_hotkey press/release
Bare modifiers match on flagsChanged keycode and pass through unconsumed
capture_next resolves next press (or bare-modifier release) to CapturedKey

flows.name: Linux inject text
steps: detect.rs picks Wayland vs X11 vs Unknown from WAYLAND_DISPLAY/DISPLAY
mod.rs sets arboard clipboard text and parses paste chord (Ctrl+V vs Ctrl+Shift+V)
X11: x11.rs resolves keysyms via server keymap and sends XTest chord
Wayland: wayland.rs uses ydotool socket if present, else wtype if in PATH
No backend available returns ClipboardOnly/Unavailable

client/crates/una-platform/src/macos/mod.rs — macOS injector: pasteboard save/restore, Cmd+V chord, frontmost app, TCC checks
client/crates/una-platform/src/macos/eventtap.rs — active CGEventTap hotkey matching and one-shot key capture
client/crates/una-platform/src/macos/axtext.rs — AX focused-field value read/write with messaging timeout
client/crates/una-platform/src/macos/keys.rs — modifier tables, key names via UCKeyTranslate, combo tokens
client/crates/una-platform/src/linux/mod.rs — Linux injector dispatch, arboard clipboard, PasteChord parsing
client/crates/una-platform/src/linux/wayland.rs — ydotool socket discovery and wtype fallback

client/crates/una-platform/src/linux/keytap.rs — X11 single-key hotkeys: XInput2 raw keys on the root (bare modifiers pass through, other keys passively grabbed), shortcut-abort window, one-shot capture for the settings recorder; lib.rs re-exports it with the Mac event tap as una_platform::hotkeys
rules: Never run AX calls on the UI thread or inside the event-tap callback; they are blocking IPC with a per-element messaging timeout.
Every axtext entry returns Option: None (terminals like Ghostty/Alacritty/kitty, canvas editors, password fields) must fall back to the correction window, never unwrap.
flagsChanged events cannot be consumed; bare-modifier hotkeys must pass through.
Active tap requires Accessibility permission already held; do not switch to listen-only semantics needing Input Monitoring.

Only una-platform compiles for Linux from the macOS dev machine ('cargo check --target aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu -p una-platform': pure Rust); build the rest on Linux (the Jetson) after changing Linux code.
Do not save/restore pasteboards larger than 10MB; always set the TransientType marker so clipboard managers skip dictation text.

Desktop shell — consumes hotkey press/release and capture results, inject outcomes, frontmost-app and permission states
Focused applications — paste target via clipboard plus synthesized chord; AX value read/write where the control publishes AXValue

cli.summary: The CLI layer is the `una` binary: a thin Clap wrapper that drives the running desktop app over its unix socket. It takes one subcommand (toggle/start/stop/cancel), maps it to a wire name, and sends it via una-core socket helpers. There is no audio, state, or server logic here — just command delivery for compositor keybinds and scripts.

flows.name: Send dictation command
steps: Parse subcommand with Clap (Toggle/Start/Stop/Cancel)
Map variant to wire name via wire_name()
Send over desktop unix socket via core helper
Exit 0 on delivery; non-zero with stderr message on failure

files: client/crates/una-cli/src/main.rs — the entire `una` binary: Clap CLI, wire-name mapping, and socket send
rules: Never add recording/transcription logic here — it only signals the running desktop app.
Wire names (toggle/start/stop/cancel) must match what the desktop shell expects; renaming breaks keybinds.
Commands are fire-and-forget no-ops when inapplicable (e.g. stop while idle); do not add blocking waits.
Failure mode is stderr message plus non-zero exit so scripts/keybinds can detect it.
edges: Desktop shell — receives the socket command and runs the actual start/stop/cancel flow
Client core — provides the unix-socket send helper the CLI calls
Platform inject — indirectly triggered downstream when dictation produces text (not touched here)

server-api.summary: The Server API layer is the FastAPI /v1 boundary for Una: routers in `api/`, Pydantic contracts in `schemas.py`, app wiring in `main.py`, config in `config.py`, shared handles in `state.py`, SQLite access in `db.py`, and typed errors in `errors.py`. A newcomer must grasp: routers are thin over services/storage/DB via `AppState`, all responses are schema-typed, and config is `una.toml` overlaid by persisted settings at startup.

flows.name: Dictation ingest
steps: POST /v1/dictations multipart audio + app_name/utterance_id hits api/dictations.py
Dedupe on utterance_id; build Whisper initial_prompt from active dictionary phrases
Transcribe via state.transcriber, clean via state.cleaner when enabled
Persist dictation row + wav via services.storage; freeze eval_holdout by ID hash
Return DictationResponse with timings, asr_model, cleanup flags

flows.name: Correction flow
steps: POST correction with corrected text for a dictation id
Validate and run training eligibility check (check_pair / edit distance)
Store corrected/polished text, eligibility, and review action in DB
Expose via detail, list, and review-queue endpoints

flows.name: Startup
steps: load_config from una.toml + UNA__SECTION__KEY env overrides
connect SQLite with WAL mode, run migrations/
apply_stored_settings overlay onto live config
Seed registry, load/warm ASR, start jobs/discovery; install error handlers

server/src/una_server/main.py — app factory, lifespan, router and static mounting
server/src/una_server/state.py — shared AppState handles (db, config, models, jobs)
server/src/una_server/db.py — aiosqlite connect, WAL pragmas, migration runner

rules: Never put sounds-like hints in the Whisper initial_prompt; bare phrases only, hints go to the cleaner.
Only keys in settings_api MUTABLE_KEYS may be changed at runtime; other config needs restart/file change.
Eval holdout is frozen at insert via is_eval_holdout ID hash; do not recompute or reassign later.

DB must stay WAL mode with busy_timeout and foreign_keys on so the training subprocess can write.
Raise typed UnaError subclasses, never raw HTTPException, to keep the {error:{code,message}} shape.

server-services.summary: This layer implements the server-side dictation pipeline: 16kHz audio ingest, faster-whisper transcription, Ollama text cleanup, active-model management, single-slot training-job launching, run eligibility, idle autotraining, and mDNS discovery. It is built as small stateless helpers plus three stateful owners (Transcriber/ModelManager, Cleaner, JobManager/Discovery) coordinated by the API layer under one inference lock. Newcomers must grasp the degradation contract: transcription is authoritative and cleanup/training must never fail or block dictation.

map.name: Moving data between servers (snapshot + idempotent merge)
Server install on x86 Linux without Docker (tenet)

flows.name: Dictation transcribe and clean
steps: storage.py decodes upload to float32 mono 16kHz and persists WAV
ModelManager lock serializes inference and hot-swaps
Transcriber runs faster-whisper in a thread and returns text plus language
Cleaner calls Ollama with system prompt from prompts.py, strips <think> tags, and bounds the call by a timeout that scales with word count
Safety check rejects output that collapses the dictation; on cleanup failure, timeout, or rejection, return raw transcript with applied=false

flows.name: Model hot-swap
steps: ModelManager looks up models row and resolves ct2_path or hf_source
Acquire inference lock to drain in-flight transcription
Free old Transcriber and GC before loading to avoid double VRAM
Construct new Transcriber for requested model and set active_model_id

flows.name: Idle auto-training
steps: autotrain.py ticks every 60s and re-reads training.auto config
Check dictation-idle time exceeds auto_idle_minutes
Check no active JobManager process and no active training_runs row
Check eligible minutes threshold and FRESH_SQL shows pairs newer than last run
Launch run via runs.launch_run so unchanged or persistently failing data never retries

rules: Dictation never fails because cleanup failed: Cleaner must degrade to raw text with applied=false, using consecutive-failure skip window.
Cleanup timeout must scale with dictation length: a flat limit sends long dictations to raw text, because the cleanup model writes about 15 words per second.
Warm the cleanup model into VRAM before real requests; cold-load blows the timeout budget and forces raw fallback.
Hold ModelManager lock for both inference and swaps, and free-then-load models to avoid double VRAM.
Never run inference on the event loop: faster-whisper transcribe runs in a thread via transcribe_sync.
Single training job only: check ACTIVE_STATUSES and JobManager.active before launch; the runner subprocess owns its training_runs row.
Autotraining must require fresh pairs newer than the last run attempt, plus idle time and eligible minutes, so it never loops on unchanged data or retries a persistently failing run.
Cleanup output that shrinks a long dictation to a short line fails the safety check and is discarded in favor of the raw transcript.

Never move a server by copying server/data over another's: it replaces the target's una.db. Use tools/merge_data.py (snapshot on the source, merge on the target), and take a last delta snapshot at cutover.
deploy/*/una.toml is caught by .gitignore's una.toml pattern: add it with git add -f or the installer ships without its defaults.

training-loop.summary: This layer fine-tunes two models from user corrections: Whisper (LoRA) for transcription and a cleanup LLM (QLoRA) for polishing style. Each side has a parallel pipeline (dataset build, train adapter, convert, evaluate, WER/edit-distance-gated promote) run as a spawned subprocess that owns its training_runs row via sync sqlite3. Newcomers must grasp that promotion only happens on a measured improvement over baseline by a margin on enough holdout samples, and that heavy ML imports must stay lazy so the serving venv stays importable.

converting: convert.merge_adapter + CTranslate2 convert + smoke test
evaluating: evaluate scores baseline vs candidate WER via CTranslate2
promoted|rejected: promote.should_promote gates registry insert and pruning

converting: style_promote.create_ollama_model via ollama create
evaluating: style_eval queries baseline and candidate via /api/chat, mean norm edit distance
promoted|rejected: should_promote_style gates live switch

rules: Keep heavy imports (torch/transformers/peft/soundfile/faster-whisper) inside functions so the serving venv can import these modules.
Stage order is fixed: building -> training -> converting -> evaluating -> promoted|rejected; eval must score converted models through the serving path (CTranslate2 / Ollama chat).
Runner sqlite uses plain sync sqlite3 with busy_timeout and foreign_keys OFF; dangling dictation->model references after pruning are accepted, do not enable FK.
Promotion requires beating baseline by >= margin on >= min_samples; never promote on training loss or vibes.
Pure-logic tests must pass without torch/transformers/peft/ollama; do not add heavy imports at module top level that break them.

The training stage runs in a spawned child via runner.in_training_process (progress via its own RunContext, PR_SET_PDEATHSIG ties it to the runner): torch keeps ~3 GB per process that empty_cache can't free, and the eval stages need it (Jetson).
Korean/code-switch data lives outside the una checkout (~/una-koen on tenet), never inside ~/una.
Korean/code-switch scripts read the una database read-only (mode=ro) and never write to it.
Korean eval runs need GPU time on tenet only after the running voice job finishes and dictation is paused, with the user's approval.
Proposed Korean mixed-script gate (not yet approved): HiKE MER must be 20 or less and under 5% of sentences may keep a wrong-script span.
Korean CER must not rise on either Korean test set; FLEURS English WER allowance (+0.3 or strict 0) is still the user's call.

ios-app.summary: A native iPhone app for Una, written in Swift and SwiftUI for iOS 17+ with no third-party packages, built with DEVELOPER_DIR=/Volumes/T7/Stockpile/Xcode.app/Contents/Developer. It records or loads 16 kHz mono WAV audio, uploads it to a user-chosen una server over HTTP, shows the transcript with copy to clipboard, and lets the user correct a past dictation from History; networking, models, corrections and WAV encoding live in the UnaKit package. A keyboard extension cannot record, so its mic key signals the containing app through an App Group flag and a Darwin notification, and the app records, uploads and returns the transcript; without an App Group (a free Apple Personal Team) the mic key shows a notice and typing still works. The idea to grasp first is that nothing is tied to one user: the server list starts empty, onboarding collects addresses, and the bundle ID and App Group live only in Config/Una.xcconfig.

The API client sends it through the endpoint race across the saved server addresses
The transcript returns; the result card shows it and copies it to the clipboard
The History tab lists past dictations

The keyboard's mic key writes a request flag to the App Group container and posts a Darwin notification

UnaKit encodes the WAV and uploads it through the endpoint race
The transcript is written to the shared container and a Darwin notification tells the keyboard

Deployment target is iOS 17.0 (app, keyboard, UnaKit); iOS 18+ APIs need `if #available`. Swift 6 mode: build off-main callbacks (the AVAudioEngine tap) in a nonisolated static func, never inline in a @MainActor type, or they trap.

DEVELOPMENT_TEAM is passed on the xcodebuild command line and never stored in the project or in Swift.
A free Personal Team cannot sign com.apple.security.application-groups, so a device build for it must drop the entitlements file and the mic handoff is unavailable.

Paid-team archives fail with an app-group profile mismatch until the App Group exists in the developer portal and is attached to both the app and keyboard App IDs; the App Store Connect API cannot create it.
TestFlight export uses manual signing with App Store profiles, because the App Manager API key cannot use Apple cloud signing and automatic export fails (steps in docs/iphone.md).
Keyboard space insertion adds nothing when the field is empty, after whitespace, or when the transcript already starts with a space.
